Title: 伊朗戰爭 (2026年)
Chunks: 31,32,33,34
3月19日，英国、法国、德国、意大利、荷兰和日本发表联合声明谴责伊朗封锁霍尔木兹海峡，并改变先前拒绝参与的立场，表示“愿为确保海峡安全通行做出适当努力。”[480]一架美国F-35战机在伊朗上空执行作战任务时，疑似遭到伊朗方面攻击而受损。该战机紧急降落在中东的美国空军基地，无人伤亡。这将是自战争爆发以来，伊首次击中美战机。[481]伊斯兰革命卫队公布了击伤该战机的视频画面。[482]
3月20日，沙特阿拉伯在北部焦夫省拦截了一枚伊朗导弹。[483]美国开始针对霍尔木兹海峡的伊朗船只和无人机进行空中打击，这是美国为重新开放该海峡进行国际航运而采取的措施之一。[484]
两栖登陆舰的出发编辑
3月20日，美军的第二艘两栖攻击舰拳击手号与第十一远征队被发现日前已经于从圣地亚哥出发前往亚洲，较预定轮换时间提前几周[485]。先前驻地日本佐世保的的黎波里号两栖攻击舰 (LHA-7)所搭载的2200名海军陆战队员11日自冲绳演练地出发后，在隔周二也被目击到穿越新加坡海峡，随后全速进入印度洋前往中东，美军此前已经对海湾的伊朗控制岛屿进行轰炸，不过此次调动并不是肯定回应，称对于是否开展地面行动仍未有定数[486]。
以色列斩首行动编辑
以色列空军在3月15日对德黑兰的空袭击毙哈塔姆安比亚中央总部情报官员阿卜杜拉·贾拉利-纳萨布和阿米尔·沙里亚特。[487][488]
3月16日，真主党旅安全指挥官阿布·阿里·阿斯卡里在巴格达的空袭中丧生。[489]

3月17日，以军在对德黑兰的空袭击毙了伊朗最高国家安全委员会秘书兼前最高领袖哈梅内伊的顾问阿里·拉里贾尼、他的儿子莫尔特扎和他的办公室主任阿里雷扎·巴亚特。[490][491]准军事组织巴斯基部队的指挥官吴拉姆-礼萨·苏莱曼尼[492]、副指挥官阿齐姆·伊斯梅利[493]和巴斯基情报局局长伊斯梅尔·艾哈迈迪也在同日被以军击毙。[494]
3月18日，以色列国防部长卡茨称以军在对德黑兰的空袭击毙了情报与国家安全部部长伊斯梅尔·哈提卜。[495][496]
3月20日，美以联军在对德黑兰东部的空袭击毙了伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队发言人阿里·穆罕默德·纳伊尼。[497]
第四周（3月21日–27日）编辑  
以色列军队在黎巴嫩边境附近（3月21日）
以色列国防部长卡茨警告说，美以联军对伊朗的打击将在第四周“显著增强”。[498]美国中央司令部司令布拉德·库珀表示，美军迄今已打击了超过8,000个伊朗军事目标，其中包括130艘舰艇。[499]

3月21日，伊朗向位于印度洋的迪戈加西亚岛英美联合军事基地发射了两枚据称是霍拉姆沙赫尔-4的远程弹道导弹：一枚导弹在飞行途中失灵、第二枚被美国军舰成功拦截。军事基地并未被击中。[500][501]美以联军继3月2日之后使用掩体炸弹第二次空袭了纳坦兹核设施[502]，伊朗袭击了以色列南部城镇迪莫纳[503]，造成至少47人受伤。伊朗声称其目标是该城市附近的内盖夫核子研究中心。[504][505]以色列南部城镇阿拉德也受袭，造成180多人受伤。[506]作为回应，以色列随后袭击了一处位于德黑兰马利克-阿什塔尔科技大学内伊朗政权用于研发核武零件的研发设施。[507]同日，一架卡塔尔军用直升机意外坠毁，造成4名卡塔尔军人、1名土耳其士兵和2名技术人员身亡。[508]
与此同时，沙特阿拉伯宣布驱逐当地伊朗大使馆的驻外武官及外交官，要求他们24小时内立即离开。[509][510]美国总统特朗普在自家社交媒体平台Truth Social上对伊朗发出最后通牒要求48小时内开放海峡，否则美军将空袭及摧毁伊朗多个发电厂[511]；伊朗则指它们会以对等手段回应美以的任何打击行动。[512]

3月22日，以军空袭了德黑兰地区的军事基地、武器生产和储存设施以及革命卫队空军的一座武器生产基地。[513]伊朗集束炸弹攻击了特拉维夫，造成15人受伤。[514]3月23日，美国总统特朗普宣布延迟空袭伊朗多个发电厂五天，称双方过去两天就彻底解决敌对行动进行了“非常好的、富有成效的对话”。受此影响，全球股市周一剧烈波动，油价下跌。[515]但随后，伊朗回应指与美国自开战以来从没有举行过任何会谈。[516]由于这不是停火或战争结束，美以联军继续轰炸德黑兰。[517]特朗普在接受CNBC采访时表示他认为“这是政权更迭，因为我正在与一些新面孔对话。”[518][519]3月24日，黎巴嫩宣布驱逐当地伊朗大使馆外交官，要求他们五天内立即离开。[520]以色列和伊朗继续互相发射导弹攻击对方[521]，以色列特拉维夫有4人轻伤。[522]伊朗官方媒体法斯通讯社报道称，美以联军对伊斯法罕两处天然气设施和一条输油管发动了空袭。[523]
3月25日，以军称在夜间空袭中轰炸了德黑兰的武器工厂；真主党称他们袭击了以色列北部的一个后勤基地；伊朗无人机袭击了科威特机场。[524]俄罗斯从伊朗布什尔核电站撤离了另外163名工作人员。[525]阿联酋国防部报告称该日是自战争爆发以来，首次没有伊朗导弹射向阿联酋[526]。伊朗革命卫队宣称击中并击落F/A-18战机，美国中央司令部X官方账号在该社交媒体平台已证实这宣称是假新闻[527]。

3月19日，英国、法国、德国、意大利、荷兰和日本发表联合声明谴责伊朗封锁霍尔木兹海峡，并改变先前拒绝参与的立场，表示“愿为确保海峡安全通行做出适当努力。”[480]一架美国F-35战机在伊朗上空执行作战任务时，疑似遭到伊朗方面攻击而受损。该战机紧急降落在中东的美国空军基地，无人伤亡。这将是自战争爆发以来，伊首次击中美战机。[481]伊斯兰革命卫队公布了击伤该战机的视频画面。[482]
3月20日，沙特阿拉伯在北部焦夫省拦截了一枚伊朗导弹。[483]美国开始针对霍尔木兹海峡的伊朗船只和无人机进行空中打击，这是美国为重新开放该海峡进行国际航运而采取的措施之一。[484]
两栖登陆舰的出发编辑
3月20日，美军的第二艘两栖攻击舰拳击手号与第十一远征队被发现日前已经于从圣地亚哥出发前往亚洲，较预定轮换时间提前几周[485]。先前驻地日本佐世保的的黎波里号两栖攻击舰 (LHA-7)所搭载的2200名海军陆战队员11日自冲绳演练地出发后，在隔周二也被目击到穿越新加坡海峡，随后全速进入印度洋前往中东，美军此前已经对海湾的伊朗控制岛屿进行轰炸，不过此次调动并不是肯定回应，称对于是否开展地面行动仍未有定数[486]。
以色列斩首行动编辑
以色列空军在3月15日对德黑兰的空袭击毙哈塔姆安比亚中央总部情报官员阿卜杜拉·贾拉利-纳萨布和阿米尔·沙里亚特。[487][488]
3月16日，真主党旅安全指挥官阿布·阿里·阿斯卡里在巴格达的空袭中丧生。[489]
texts.32:
3月17日，以军在对德黑兰的空袭击毙了伊朗最高国家安全委员会秘书兼前最高领袖哈梅内伊的顾问阿里·拉里贾尼、他的儿子莫尔特扎和他的办公室主任阿里雷扎·巴亚特。[490][491]准军事组织巴斯基部队的指挥官吴拉姆-礼萨·苏莱曼尼[492]、副指挥官阿齐姆·伊斯梅利[493]和巴斯基情报局局长伊斯梅尔·艾哈迈迪也在同日被以军击毙。[494]
3月18日，以色列国防部长卡茨称以军在对德黑兰的空袭击毙了情报与国家安全部部长伊斯梅尔·哈提卜。[495][496]
3月20日，美以联军在对德黑兰东部的空袭击毙了伊朗伊斯兰革命卫队发言人阿里·穆罕默德·纳伊尼。[497]
第四周（3月21日–27日）编辑  
以色列军队在黎巴嫩边境附近（3月21日）
以色列国防部长卡茨警告说，美以联军对伊朗的打击将在第四周“显著增强”。[498]美国中央司令部司令布拉德·库珀表示，美军迄今已打击了超过8,000个伊朗军事目标，其中包括130艘舰艇。[499]
texts.33:
3月21日，伊朗向位于印度洋的迪戈加西亚岛英美联合军事基地发射了两枚据称是霍拉姆沙赫尔-4的远程弹道导弹：一枚导弹在飞行途中失灵、第二枚被美国军舰成功拦截。军事基地并未被击中。[500][501]美以联军继3月2日之后使用掩体炸弹第二次空袭了纳坦兹核设施[502]，伊朗袭击了以色列南部城镇迪莫纳[503]，造成至少47人受伤。伊朗声称其目标是该城市附近的内盖夫核子研究中心。[504][505]以色列南部城镇阿拉德也受袭，造成180多人受伤。[506]作为回应，以色列随后袭击了一处位于德黑兰马利克-阿什塔尔科技大学内伊朗政权用于研发核武零件的研发设施。[507]同日，一架卡塔尔军用直升机意外坠毁，造成4名卡塔尔军人、1名土耳其士兵和2名技术人员身亡。[508]
与此同时，沙特阿拉伯宣布驱逐当地伊朗大使馆的驻外武官及外交官，要求他们24小时内立即离开。[509][510]美国总统特朗普在自家社交媒体平台Truth Social上对伊朗发出最后通牒要求48小时内开放海峡，否则美军将空袭及摧毁伊朗多个发电厂[511]；伊朗则指它们会以对等手段回应美以的任何打击行动。[512]
texts.34:
3月22日，以军空袭了德黑兰地区的军事基地、武器生产和储存设施以及革命卫队空军的一座武器生产基地。[513]伊朗集束炸弹攻击了特拉维夫，造成15人受伤。[514]3月23日，美国总统特朗普宣布延迟空袭伊朗多个发电厂五天，称双方过去两天就彻底解决敌对行动进行了“非常好的、富有成效的对话”。受此影响，全球股市周一剧烈波动，油价下跌。[515]但随后，伊朗回应指与美国自开战以来从没有举行过任何会谈。[516]由于这不是停火或战争结束，美以联军继续轰炸德黑兰。[517]特朗普在接受CNBC采访时表示他认为“这是政权更迭，因为我正在与一些新面孔对话。”[518][519]3月24日，黎巴嫩宣布驱逐当地伊朗大使馆外交官，要求他们五天内立即离开。[520]以色列和伊朗继续互相发射导弹攻击对方[521]，以色列特拉维夫有4人轻伤。[522]伊朗官方媒体法斯通讯社报道称，美以联军对伊斯法罕两处天然气设施和一条输油管发动了空袭。[523]
3月25日，以军称在夜间空袭中轰炸了德黑兰的武器工厂；真主党称他们袭击了以色列北部的一个后勤基地；伊朗无人机袭击了科威特机场。[524]俄罗斯从伊朗布什尔核电站撤离了另外163名工作人员。[525]阿联酋国防部报告称该日是自战争爆发以来，首次没有伊朗导弹射向阿联酋[526]。伊朗革命卫队宣称击中并击落F/A-18战机，美国中央司令部X官方账号在该社交媒体平台已证实这宣称是假新闻[527]。

TAIPEI, Taiwan—A Chinese asylum-seeker posing as a policeman and accompanied by his family hijacked a Chinese airliner to Taiwan on Friday, the 11th such hijacking since April.
Taiwan detained the man for trial on air piracy charges. But in a break with previous practice, it forcibly sent the four family members who had traveled with him--his foster mother, wife and two sons, aged 8 and 10--back to China.
Lin Wenqiang, 35, dressed in the uniform of a Chinese policeman, used a fruit knife and a fake bomb--a teacup stuffed with toilet paper--to force a China Southwest Airlines Boeing 737 to Taipei.

He surrendered to Taiwan authorities and requested asylum for himself and his family. The plane and its crew members and other passengers, including Lin’s family, were sent back to China four hours later.

It was the first time that Taiwan had forcibly repatriated family members not accused of air piracy.

## Flying a helicopter in fog can be a recipe for disaster — Kobe Bryant and now Iran's president add to a string of deaths
ByThibault Spirlet
You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.
Getty Images A composite image of Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi and Kobe Bryant.
May 20, 2024, 11:01 AM UTC
Flying a helicopter in fog can be a recipe for disaster, with Kobe Bryant and now Iran's president adding to a string of deaths.
Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi and his entourage died after his aircraft crashed Sunday in a remote and mountainous area of northwestern Iran.
The group was on a helicopter ride back from a ceremony marking a dam opening near Azerbaijan's border when it crashed into trees in the region of Iran's East Azerbaijan province, [per Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/5/20/live-irans-president-raisi-fm-amirabdollahian-killed-in-helicopter-crash#:~:text=Iran's%20President%20Ebrahim%20Raisi%20and,northern%20Iran's%20East%20Azerbaijan%20province.).
Interior Minister Ahmad Vahidi told IRNA, Iran's state-run news agency, that the helicopter carrying Raisi and other senior Iranian officials was forced to make a "hard landing" Sunday but failed to offer details.
The search was "extremely difficult" because of darkness, dense fog, and rain, Pirhossein Koulivand, the head of Iran's Emergency Medical Services, said on Iranian state TV about 10 hours into the operation, per Bloomberg.
State TV said the helicopter crashed into a mountain. While there is no official statement on the cause, images of the crash site captured by ISNA, Iran's state students' news agency, showed heavy fog lingering over the area.
According to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, flying in fog is challenging, even for the most experienced of pilots. "For pilots that are not as skilled, fog is an extremely dangerous and potentially deadly hazard," it said.
Raisi's helicopter crash follows a series of deadly helicopter and plane crashes in foggy weather conditions.

## Flying a helicopter in fog can be a recipe for disaster — Kobe Bryant and now Iran's president add to a string of deaths
Last year, a helicopter carrying Ukraine's interior minister crashed into a kindergarten in a foggy residential suburb of Kyiv, claiming his life and that of a dozen people, authorities said at the time, per The Associated Press.
India's top military official, Gen. Bipin Rawat, and his wife perished with 11 other passengers in December 2021 after their helicopter flew unusually low and through heavy fog before crashing into a hillside in southern India, eyewitnesses told Reuters at the time.
In January 2020, Kobe Bryant's helicopter crashed in foggy conditions while en route from John Wayne Airport to Camarillo Airport, killing the NBA legend, his then-13-year-old daughter, the Orange Coast College baseball coach John Altobelli, and his family. The pilot of the helicopter most likely became disorientated amid fog, US safety investigators said.
Ten years earlier, Polish President Lech Kaczynski, the first lady, and 94 others died in a plane crash after pilots tried to land in thick fog with reduced visibility near the western Russian city of Smolensk, according to a final report by the country's committee for Investigation on National Aviation Accidents.
In 1994, a Chinook Mk2 helicopter carrying 25 senior British intelligence experts crashed into the hillside on the Mull of Kintyre in southwestern Scotland after the pilot flew too fast and too low in foggy conditions, killing all passengers on board, the UK's Defence Committee said at the time.
Raisi's body and those of the other passengers who died in the helicopter crash are being transported to the city of Tabriz, where an autopsy will take place, followed by a first official state funeral on Tuesday, according to Al Jazeera.

United States Army[223] - The U.S. Army has a stated requirement for 2,135 aircraft.[257] The service operates 19 HH-60Ls, 346 HH-60Ms (medevac), 20 UH-60As (estimated), 800 UH-60Ls, 931 UH-60Ms, and 90 UH-60Vs as of January 2025.[258]: 37   
United States Navy (see SH-60)  
United States Coast Guard (see MH-60)

United States Department of State  
United States Department of Homeland Security  
Florida State Guard - By the end of 2024, the Florida State Guard purchased two UH-60 Black Hawk helicopters.[259][260]  
Former operatorsedit  
 Islamic Republic of Afghanistan - 2014 until August 2021  
Afghan Air Force  
 British Hong Kong  
Royal Hong Kong Auxiliary Air Force[211][261]  
Government Flying Service[262]  
Accidentsedit  
For accidents involving other Japanese H-60 helicopters, see Mitsubishi H-60 § Accidents.  
From 1981 to 1987, five Black Hawks crashed (killing or injuring all on board) while flying near radio broadcast towers because their electromagnetic emissions disrupted the helicopters' flight control systems. The Black Hawk helicopters were not hardened against high-intensity radiated fields, contrary to the SH-60 Seahawk Navy variant. The pilots were instructed to fly away from emitters, and, in the long term, shielding was increased and backup systems were installed.[263]  
On 29 July 1992, one Australian Army Black Hawk collided into terrain near Oakey Army Aviation Centre, killing two occupants.[264]  

On 3 March 1994, a UH-60 helicopter of the 15th Fighter Wing, Republic of Korea Air Force (ROKAF) exploded above Yongin, Gyeonggi-do, killing all six personnel on board; among those killed was General Cho Kun-hae, then Chief of the Air Staff of South Korea.[265]  
On 14 April 1994, two U.S. Army UH-60 Black Hawks in northern Iraq were shot down in a friendly fire incident by U.S. Air Force F-15 fighter jets patrolling the northern no-fly zone that had been imposed after the 1991 Gulf War, in which all twenty-six crew and passengers were killed. The pilots of the U.S. Air Force F-15s misidentified the U.S. Army Black Hawk helicopters as enemy Mil Mi-24 "Hind" helicopters.[266]  
On 12 June 1996, two Australian Army Black Hawks collided during an Army nighttime special forces counter-terrorism exercise resulting in the death of eighteen soldiers - fifteen members of the SASR and three from the 5th Aviation Regiment.[267][268][269]  
On 12 February 2001, two Black Hawks from Schofield Barracks, Hawaii collided during NVG formation flight training, causing loss of both aircraft, six deaths and 11 injured soldiers.[270]  
On 12 February 2004, one Australian Army Black Hawk collided into terrain in the vicinity of Mount Walker, Queensland following contact between the tail rotor and a tree. The airframe was written off however there were no deaths - six out of the eight occupants received injuries.[271][272]  
Aftermath of a crashed UH-60 in 2004, at Tallil Airbase, Iraq  
On 26 September 2004, a U.S. Army Black Hawk crashed taking off from Tallil Airbase (Nasiriyah Airport), Iraq. The crew of four was rescued.[273]  

On 29 November 2006, one Australian Army Black Hawk crashed into and subsequently slid off the deck of HMAS Kanimbla sinking into deep waters off the coast of Fiji while conducting a training flight. The sinking resulted in the deaths of two soldiers - one pilot from the 5th Aviation Regiment, and one trooper from the SASR.[274][275]  
On 10 March 2015, a UH-60 from Eglin Air Force Base crashed off the coast of the Florida Panhandle near the base. All eleven on board were killed.[276]  
On 16 February 2018, a UH-60M helicopter deployed by the Mexican Air Force to Oaxaca after an earthquake, crashed while attempting to land, all 4 occupants on board survived but 14 people on the ground were killed.[277][278]  
On 2 January 2020, a UH-60M helicopter of the Republic of China Air Force (ROCAF) in Taiwan, crashed on a mountainside, killing eight people on board, including General Shen Yi-ming, chief of the general staff of Republic of China's armed forces.[279]  
On 23 June 2021, a Philippine Air Force S-70i crashed in Capas town in Tarlac during a night flight training, killing all 6 crew members. The unit was newly delivered in November of the previous year or only almost 8 months old.[280]  
On 22 February 2022, two Utah National Guard Black Hawk helicopters crashed at the Snowbird, Utah ski resort during a training exercise. One Black Hawk was overcome by whiteout conditions caused by the downdraft in the snow, and crashed, causing parts of the rotor blades to strike the other helicopter, forcing a hard landing. There were no major injuries to the crew or skiers.[281]  
On July 16, 2022, one Mexican Navy Black Hawk crashed at Sinaloa, killing 14 of the 15 marines on board.[282]  
In September 2022, a Black Hawk operated by the Taliban crashed during a training exercise in Kabul, killing three.[283]  

On February 15, 2023, a Black Hawk crashed killing two members of the Tennessee National Guard in Huntsville, Alabama.[284]  
On 29 March 2023, two US Army Black Hawk medical helicopters collided during a training mission over Kentucky. All nine soldiers aboard were killed. The cause of the crash is under investigation.[285][286]  
The wreckage of UH-60L 00-26860, operating as Priority Air Transport 25, after the collision into the Potomac River, Washington, D.C. in 2025.  
On 10 November 2023, a US Army Black Hawk crashed off the coast of Cyprus in the Mediterranean Sea. All 5 soldiers aboard were killed.[287]  
On 11 September 2024, an Israel Defense Forces (IDF) Black Hawk crashed in Rafah, Gaza during a medical evacuation mission. Two soldiers were killed, and seven others were injured.[288]  
On 29 January 2025, a U.S. Army UH-60L Black Hawk from the 12th Aviation Battalion operating as Priority Air Transport 25 collided with American Eagle Flight 5342 near Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport sending both aircraft crashing into the Potomac River. All 64 aboard the plane and all three aboard the helicopter were killed.[289]

## Flying a helicopter in fog can be a recipe for disaster — Kobe Bryant and now Iran's president add to a string of deaths
ByThibault Spirlet
You're currently following this author! Click to unsubscribe from email alerts.
Getty Images A composite image of Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi and Kobe Bryant.
May 20, 2024, 11:01 AM UTC
Flying a helicopter in fog can be a recipe for disaster, with Kobe Bryant and now Iran's president adding to a string of deaths.
Iranian President Ebrahim Raisi and his entourage died after his aircraft crashed Sunday in a remote and mountainous area of northwestern Iran.
The group was on a helicopter ride back from a ceremony marking a dam opening near Azerbaijan's border when it crashed into trees in the region of Iran's East Azerbaijan province, [per Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/liveblog/2024/5/20/live-irans-president-raisi-fm-amirabdollahian-killed-in-helicopter-crash#:~:text=Iran's%20President%20Ebrahim%20Raisi%20and,northern%20Iran's%20East%20Azerbaijan%20province.).
Interior Minister Ahmad Vahidi told IRNA, Iran's state-run news agency, that the helicopter carrying Raisi and other senior Iranian officials was forced to make a "hard landing" Sunday but failed to offer details.
The search was "extremely difficult" because of darkness, dense fog, and rain, Pirhossein Koulivand, the head of Iran's Emergency Medical Services, said on Iranian state TV about 10 hours into the operation, per Bloomberg.
State TV said the helicopter crashed into a mountain. While there is no official statement on the cause, images of the crash site captured by ISNA, Iran's state students' news agency, showed heavy fog lingering over the area.
According to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, flying in fog is challenging, even for the most experienced of pilots. "For pilots that are not as skilled, fog is an extremely dangerous and potentially deadly hazard," it said.
Raisi's helicopter crash follows a series of deadly helicopter and plane crashes in foggy weather conditions.

## Flying a helicopter in fog can be a recipe for disaster — Kobe Bryant and now Iran's president add to a string of deaths
Last year, a helicopter carrying Ukraine's interior minister crashed into a kindergarten in a foggy residential suburb of Kyiv, claiming his life and that of a dozen people, authorities said at the time, per The Associated Press.
India's top military official, Gen. Bipin Rawat, and his wife perished with 11 other passengers in December 2021 after their helicopter flew unusually low and through heavy fog before crashing into a hillside in southern India, eyewitnesses told Reuters at the time.
In January 2020, Kobe Bryant's helicopter crashed in foggy conditions while en route from John Wayne Airport to Camarillo Airport, killing the NBA legend, his then-13-year-old daughter, the Orange Coast College baseball coach John Altobelli, and his family. The pilot of the helicopter most likely became disorientated amid fog, US safety investigators said.
Ten years earlier, Polish President Lech Kaczynski, the first lady, and 94 others died in a plane crash after pilots tried to land in thick fog with reduced visibility near the western Russian city of Smolensk, according to a final report by the country's committee for Investigation on National Aviation Accidents.
In 1994, a Chinook Mk2 helicopter carrying 25 senior British intelligence experts crashed into the hillside on the Mull of Kintyre in southwestern Scotland after the pilot flew too fast and too low in foggy conditions, killing all passengers on board, the UK's Defence Committee said at the time.
Raisi's body and those of the other passengers who died in the helicopter crash are being transported to the city of Tabriz, where an autopsy will take place, followed by a first official state funeral on Tuesday, according to Al Jazeera.

For accidents involving other Japanese H-60 helicopters, see Mitsubishi H-60 § Accidents.  
From 1981 to 1987, five Black Hawks crashed (killing or injuring all on board) while flying near radio broadcast towers because their electromagnetic emissions disrupted the helicopters' flight control systems. The Black Hawk helicopters were not hardened against high-intensity radiated fields, contrary to the SH-60 Seahawk Navy variant. The pilots were instructed to fly away from emitters, and, in the long term, shielding was increased and backup systems were installed.[263]  
On 29 July 1992, one Australian Army Black Hawk collided into terrain near Oakey Army Aviation Centre, killing two occupants.[264]  

On 3 March 1994, a UH-60 helicopter of the 15th Fighter Wing, Republic of Korea Air Force (ROKAF) exploded above Yongin, Gyeonggi-do, killing all six personnel on board; among those killed was General Cho Kun-hae, then Chief of the Air Staff of South Korea.[265]  
On 14 April 1994, two U.S. Army UH-60 Black Hawks in northern Iraq were shot down in a friendly fire incident by U.S. Air Force F-15 fighter jets patrolling the northern no-fly zone that had been imposed after the 1991 Gulf War, in which all twenty-six crew and passengers were killed. On 29 November 2006, one Australian Army Black Hawk crashed into and subsequently slid off the deck of HMAS Kanimbla sinking into deep waters off the coast of Fiji while conducting a training flight. On 10 March 2015, a UH-60 from Eglin Air Force Base crashed off the coast of the Florida Panhandle near the base. All eleven on board were killed.[276]  
On 16 February 2018, a UH-60M helicopter deployed by the Mexican Air Force to Oaxaca after an earthquake, crashed while attempting to land, all 4 occupants on board survived but 14 people on the ground were killed.[277][278]

The pilot of the helicopter most likely became disorientated amid fog, US safety investigators said.
Ten years earlier, Polish President Lech Kaczynski, the first lady, and 94 others died in a plane crash after pilots tried to land in thick fog with reduced visibility near the western Russian city of Smolensk, according to a final report by the country's committee for Investigation on National Aviation Accidents.
In 1994, a Chinook Mk2 helicopter carrying 25 senior British intelligence experts crashed into the hillside on the Mull of Kintyre in southwestern Scotland after the pilot flew too fast and too low in foggy conditions, killing all passengers on board, the UK's Defence Committee said at the time.

Title: FDS Helicopter Crash Sparks Anger: Indemnity Form, RM30 Allowance
Chunks: 0,1,2
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Yesterday’s crash of a Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter in Sarawak, which killed all five people on board, has triggered anger among Ministry of Health (MOH) staff and the public.
On social media, many shared the low Air Health Service Incentive Payment allowance, which was created in 1978, that pays medical officers, assistant medical officers, nurses, and community nurses only RM30 for a return flight.
Dr Justine Sim, who works in public service, said he accompanied a patient with a complete heart block by helicopter from Miri Hospital to the Sarawak Heart Centre in 2018.
“I did not even know this RM30 allowance existed. Nobody told me. Nobody asked me to claim it either. But RM30 is actually not the most disturbing part,” he posted on Facebook.
“Before that flight, I received no dedicated aviation safety training. No structured emergency evacuation training. No proper briefing on brace position, rotor hazards, fire, hard landing or what to do if the aircraft itself became the emergency. No dedicated aviation risk insurance protection was explained to me either. Basically? _Terus masuk helicopter & fly.”_
Another person posted on Threads that the question wasn’t about asking for a higher allowance, but “an acknowledgement appropriate for the responsibility and risk”.
Dr Sim disclosed an indemnity form, which he had to sign before serving on the FDS, that indemnifies the Malaysian government, Malaysian Armed Forces, or any Commonwealth Armed Forces from any legal claim or action brought by the person signing it, their next-of-kin, or their estate in the event of injury, disability, or death during travel on an aircraft, ship, or car managed by the armed forces.
The government doctor said the MOH and Public Service Department (JPA) shouldn’t simply increase the RM30 allowance to RM40 and boast of a 33.3 per cent hike.
“Review the whole arrangement — the allowance, safety training, occupational risk insurance, compensation, emergency preparedness and the indemnity paperwork health care workers are required to sign before flying,” said Dr Sim.
“Five people died while carrying out a health care mission. Perhaps this is the moment to ask who exactly this system is designed to protect.”

A copy of an indemnity certificate that health care workers must sign before getting onto a Flying Doctor Service helicopter. Photo by Dr Justine Sim.
The victims of the helicopter crash yesterday afternoon were a pilot and four health care workers in the MOH on official duty: Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, a 33-year-old female medical officer from Kelantan, as well as an assistant medical officer and two nurses.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) said in a brief statement yesterday that the crash involved a BO-105 helicopter, with a 9M-LLF registration number, and that the incident will be probed by the Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) under the Ministry of Transport.
_The Borneo Post_ reported that the helicopter was flying from Miri Airport to Long Lellang when it crashed at the Long Lellang STOLport in the interior of Baram. CAAM said it received notification of the incident at 3.58pm yesterday.
Videos posted on social media showed the helicopter on fire in the sky before it crashed.
Others have questioned the age of the helicopter, posting an AI answer that the MBB BO-105 helicopter model went on its first flight in 1967 in Germany, with manufacturing from 1967 to 2001.
A Malaysian posted on Threads that at a time when the country’s leaders and high-ranked civil servants fly on modern and well-maintained aircraft, “the country’s heroes take a risk in flying on ancient and dilapidated aircraft for the sake of responsibility.”
“Don’t the minister, KSU (secretary-general), and Health director-general feel guilty? Don’t you all have a heart? These are human lives. The people have lost the country’s heroes,” he wrote.
Many commenting on Health Minister Dzulkefly Ahmad’s Facebook post of his condolences to the victims similarly expressed anger.
“Some say that that helicopter was 35 years old, whereas others say it was 50 years old. Whatever the real age of the helicopter, the MOH must take responsibility and provide appropriate compensation for the families of the victims for losing their loved ones,” a woman wrote.
“At the same time, ensure that helicopters used after this are truly verified to be safe and fulfil all safety requirements. This facility is very important, especially for the interiors that are hard to reach on road or river.”

Another person posted that an RM30 allowance was “highly inappropriate” for risking one’s life for patients living in the interiors.
A government doctor wrote: “Black day for KKM.”
MOH provides FDS and Medical Evacuation (Medevac) services for Sabah, Sarawak, and the Orang Asli residing in rural areas in Perak and Kelantan.
Dr Sangeetha Siniah, a paediatrician and specialist in infectious disease, allergy, and immunology, recalled her Medevac helicopter rides in Sarawak.
“Once, we had to get an emergency landing, it was so scary. Only after that I actually bought life insurance,” she posted on X.
Retired paediatrician Dr Amar-Singh HSS posted on X that he previously transported ill children by Medevac helicopters in Sarawak.
“Remember once getting caught in a storm and an emergency landing in a field. Frightening. Had to continue ventilating the child (ambu bag & ETT).”

Title: Pilot and four medical workers killed in air ambulance helicopter crash amid Borneo wildfires
Chunks: 0,1
Five people died when a "flying doctor" service helicopter crashed in Malaysia on Tuesday, authorities said, as haze from Indonesianwildfires complicated search efforts.
Health minister, Dzulkefly Ahmad, said in a statement that initial information showed a pilot and four health ministry staff were aboard the helicopter when it crashed near Long Lellang short take-off and landing airport in Sarawak, on the island of Borneo.
Those on board included a medical officer, an assistant medical officer, and two nurses who were on official duty, he said.
This aerial photo taken from a commercial aircraft shows haze from Indonesian forest fires blanketing a bridge in Kuching, the capital city of Malaysia's Sarawak state on the island of Borneo on September 5, 2026 (AFP/Getty)
A disaster management committee official in Miri, Sarawak, confirmed to the state news agency Bernama that all five people aboard had died in the crash.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia said the helicopter, a Bo-105, was carrying five people when it crashed after the Flight Information Service notified the authority of the incident at 3.58pm the previous day.
Investigators from the Air Accident Investigation Bureau are expected to arrive in Miri at 2pm on Wednesday to begin examining the crash, according to the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia's chief executive, Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud, quoted by the _New Straits Times_.
"The helicopter wreckage at the crash site will remain undisturbed following instructions from the AAIB," he said. "The site has been cordoned off and secured."
Search and recovery operations were set to resume on Wednesday, with a Fire and Rescue Department helicopter carrying 18 personnel departing Miri for Long Lellang at 7am.
A teacher communicates with students on her phone while standing in the compounds of her school seen shrouded in smog after local authorities mandated remote learning due to haze from land and forest fires in Pontianak, West Kalimantan (AFP/Getty)
Two police helicopters carrying 11 personnel were due to join the operation, along with four police officers from Long Lama and four Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency personnel from Miri. Police are expected to oversee the identification of victims at Miri Hospital, including DNA comparisons with their families.
Malaysia's "flying doctor" service typically uses aircraft to provide medical care, emergency transport, and clinical services to rural or isolated regions.

Search operations on Tuesday were hampered by hazy conditions, with rescuers barred from using air services, Sarawak police commissioner Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said in a statement. He added that the crash site was in a remote area requiring a ten-hour journey by road.
Sarawak has been badly affected by haze from forest fires in neighbouring Indonesia, with many areas recording unhealthy air quality levels, according to government data released on Wednesday. Malaysia declared an emergency last week in Sarawak's Serian district after air pollution reached hazardous levels, though the declaration was lifted after air quality improved.

Five people died when a "flying doctor" service helicopter crashed in Malaysia on Tuesday, authorities said, as haze from Indonesianwildfires complicated search efforts.
Health minister, Dzulkefly Ahmad, said in a statement that initial information showed a pilot and four health ministry staff were aboard the helicopter when it crashed near Long Lellang short take-off and landing airport in Sarawak, on the island of Borneo.
Those on board included a medical officer, an assistant medical officer, and two nurses who were on official duty, he said.
This aerial photo taken from a commercial aircraft shows haze from Indonesian forest fires blanketing a bridge in Kuching, the capital city of Malaysia's Sarawak state on the island of Borneo on September 5, 2026 (AFP/Getty)
A disaster management committee official in Miri, Sarawak, confirmed to the state news agency Bernama that all five people aboard had died in the crash.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia said the helicopter, a Bo-105, was carrying five people when it crashed after the Flight Information Service notified the authority of the incident at 3.58pm the previous day.
Investigators from the Air Accident Investigation Bureau are expected to arrive in Miri at 2pm on Wednesday to begin examining the crash, according to the Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia's chief executive, Datuk Captain Norazman Mahmud, quoted by the _New Straits Times_.
"The helicopter wreckage at the crash site will remain undisturbed following instructions from the AAIB," he said. "The site has been cordoned off and secured."
Search and recovery operations were set to resume on Wednesday, with a Fire and Rescue Department helicopter carrying 18 personnel departing Miri for Long Lellang at 7am.
A teacher communicates with students on her phone while standing in the compounds of her school seen shrouded in smog after local authorities mandated remote learning due to haze from land and forest fires in Pontianak, West Kalimantan (AFP/Getty)
Two police helicopters carrying 11 personnel were due to join the operation, along with four police officers from Long Lama and four Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency personnel from Miri. Police are expected to oversee the identification of victims at Miri Hospital, including DNA comparisons with their families.
Malaysia's "flying doctor" service typically uses aircraft to provide medical care, emergency transport, and clinical services to rural or isolated regions.

Search operations on Tuesday were hampered by hazy conditions, with rescuers barred from using air services, Sarawak police commissioner Mohamad Zainal Abdullah said in a statement. He added that the crash site was in a remote area requiring a ten-hour journey by road.
Sarawak has been badly affected by haze from forest fires in neighbouring Indonesia, with many areas recording unhealthy air quality levels, according to government data released on Wednesday. Malaysia declared an emergency last week in Sarawak's Serian district after air pollution reached hazardous levels, though the declaration was lifted after air quality improved.

Title: FDS Helicopter Crash Sparks Anger: Indemnity Form, RM30 Allowance
Chunks: 0,1,2
KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 9 — Yesterday’s crash of a Flying Doctor Service (FDS) helicopter in Sarawak, which killed all five people on board, has triggered anger among Ministry of Health (MOH) staff and the public.
On social media, many shared the low Air Health Service Incentive Payment allowance, which was created in 1978, that pays medical officers, assistant medical officers, nurses, and community nurses only RM30 for a return flight.
Dr Justine Sim, who works in public service, said he accompanied a patient with a complete heart block by helicopter from Miri Hospital to the Sarawak Heart Centre in 2018.
“I did not even know this RM30 allowance existed. Nobody told me. Nobody asked me to claim it either. But RM30 is actually not the most disturbing part,” he posted on Facebook.
“Before that flight, I received no dedicated aviation safety training. No structured emergency evacuation training. No proper briefing on brace position, rotor hazards, fire, hard landing or what to do if the aircraft itself became the emergency. No dedicated aviation risk insurance protection was explained to me either. Basically? _Terus masuk helicopter & fly.”_
Another person posted on Threads that the question wasn’t about asking for a higher allowance, but “an acknowledgement appropriate for the responsibility and risk”.
Dr Sim disclosed an indemnity form, which he had to sign before serving on the FDS, that indemnifies the Malaysian government, Malaysian Armed Forces, or any Commonwealth Armed Forces from any legal claim or action brought by the person signing it, their next-of-kin, or their estate in the event of injury, disability, or death during travel on an aircraft, ship, or car managed by the armed forces.
The government doctor said the MOH and Public Service Department (JPA) shouldn’t simply increase the RM30 allowance to RM40 and boast of a 33.3 per cent hike.
“Review the whole arrangement — the allowance, safety training, occupational risk insurance, compensation, emergency preparedness and the indemnity paperwork health care workers are required to sign before flying,” said Dr Sim.
“Five people died while carrying out a health care mission. Perhaps this is the moment to ask who exactly this system is designed to protect.”

A copy of an indemnity certificate that health care workers must sign before getting onto a Flying Doctor Service helicopter. Photo by Dr Justine Sim.
The victims of the helicopter crash yesterday afternoon were a pilot and four health care workers in the MOH on official duty: Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, a 33-year-old female medical officer from Kelantan, as well as an assistant medical officer and two nurses.
The Civil Aviation Authority of Malaysia (CAAM) said in a brief statement yesterday that the crash involved a BO-105 helicopter, with a 9M-LLF registration number, and that the incident will be probed by the Air Accident Investigation Bureau (AAIB) under the Ministry of Transport.
_The Borneo Post_ reported that the helicopter was flying from Miri Airport to Long Lellang when it crashed at the Long Lellang STOLport in the interior of Baram. CAAM said it received notification of the incident at 3.58pm yesterday.
Videos posted on social media showed the helicopter on fire in the sky before it crashed.
Others have questioned the age of the helicopter, posting an AI answer that the MBB BO-105 helicopter model went on its first flight in 1967 in Germany, with manufacturing from 1967 to 2001.
A Malaysian posted on Threads that at a time when the country’s leaders and high-ranked civil servants fly on modern and well-maintained aircraft, “the country’s heroes take a risk in flying on ancient and dilapidated aircraft for the sake of responsibility.”
“Don’t the minister, KSU (secretary-general), and Health director-general feel guilty? Don’t you all have a heart? These are human lives. The people have lost the country’s heroes,” he wrote.
Many commenting on Health Minister Dzulkefly Ahmad’s Facebook post of his condolences to the victims similarly expressed anger.
“Some say that that helicopter was 35 years old, whereas others say it was 50 years old. Whatever the real age of the helicopter, the MOH must take responsibility and provide appropriate compensation for the families of the victims for losing their loved ones,” a woman wrote.
“At the same time, ensure that helicopters used after this are truly verified to be safe and fulfil all safety requirements. This facility is very important, especially for the interiors that are hard to reach on road or river.”

Another person posted that an RM30 allowance was “highly inappropriate” for risking one’s life for patients living in the interiors.
A government doctor wrote: “Black day for KKM.”
MOH provides FDS and Medical Evacuation (Medevac) services for Sabah, Sarawak, and the Orang Asli residing in rural areas in Perak and Kelantan.
Dr Sangeetha Siniah, a paediatrician and specialist in infectious disease, allergy, and immunology, recalled her Medevac helicopter rides in Sarawak.
“Once, we had to get an emergency landing, it was so scary. Only after that I actually bought life insurance,” she posted on X.
Retired paediatrician Dr Amar-Singh HSS posted on X that he previously transported ill children by Medevac helicopters in Sarawak.
“Remember once getting caught in a storm and an emergency landing in a field. Frightening. Had to continue ventilating the child (ambu bag & ETT).”
